metadata.note: The St. Johnsbury - Swanton - Maquam line in northern Vermont (Montpelier & St. Johnsbury and Lamoille Valley railroads, jointly managed as the Portland & Ogdensburg's Vermont Division, then from 1 Jul 1880 the St. Johnsbury & Lake Champlain, reorganized 1948 as the St. Johnsbury & Lamoille County), plus the Hardwick & Woodbury granite road. The P&O era is drawn as four features split at the documented opening stages (1872 / 1873 / 1876 / 1877) plus Swanton - Maquam; the StJ&LC era is one main-line feature on the identical concatenated geometry (Rule 4 split at 1 Jul 1880) plus Swanton - Maquam. The 1948 reorganization is NOT split. St. Johnsbury - Lunenburg (the Essex County RR, operated by the Maine Central from 1912) is left to maine_central_mountain_division.geojson, which already draws that track.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing drawn after passenger service. Not drawn: the 1956 - c.1994 freight afterlife (StJ&LCo to 1973; State of Vermont / Vermont Northern / Lamoille Valley Railroad Co. from 1 Jan 1978, washouts 1995/97); Hardwick & Woodbury freight 1922 - 1934; the Granite / Hardwick branch before the H&W era; the Victory branch (a logging road with a single 1889 passenger-guide listing, omitted as too thin to draw).
metadata.line_label_audit: Labels written to Rule 6 at creation.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END: Swanton - Maquam (st-johnsbury-lake-champlain-swanton-maquam) confirmed only to 1894 (Pathfinder, via Fowler); Maquam is on B&M agency lists 1906 and 1918 but not 1923 - agency lists, not passenger evidence. When passenger service to Maquam ended is unknown.

Who ran the main line 1912-1927? Wikipedia (Portland and Ogdensburg Railway) says the Maine Central leased 'the old Vermont Division' in July 1912 and cut the lease back to east of St. Johnsbury on 1 Aug 1927; Wikipedia (Morrisville station) says the MEC lease on Morrisville's rails held until 1927. The ICC valuation (property as of 30 Jun 1916) names the MEC as operator of Lunenburg - St. Johnsbury only, and the B&M's 1914/1918/1923 agency lists carry St. Johnsbury - Swanton under the StJ&LC. Drawn per the ICC (no split). A 1912-1927 public timetable would settle it; if MEC-operated trains west of St. Johnsbury are shown, split the main line at those dates.

B&M stock control vs operation c.1887-1925: the ICC abstract describes control 'through ownership of ... stock and voting rights' with some equipment leased; a 1915 St. Johnsbury Caledonian obituary calls the StJ&LC a 'division of the Boston and Maine' c.1895-1913, and american-rails.com speaks of a mid-1920s return to 'independent management'. Read as stock control (no split). A B&M public timetable printing St. Johnsbury - Swanton as a B&M division table would reverse that.

Exact 1956 end date: Wikipedia, american-rails.com and VTrans give only the year. Likely print sources: Philip R. Hastings, 'St. Johnsbury & Lake Champlain', Trains, May 1947; Nimke, 'Connecticut River Railroad and Connections' vol. VIII.

1930s cutback: VAST's LVRT history says passengers 'through the 1930s' ran only Cambridge - St. Johnsbury. Unsourced and contradicted for 1951 by the Official Guide; not drawn as a gap. If substantiated as a real suspension, split Cambridge Junction - Swanton around it.
Hardwick - Johnson opening: ICC '1876' (drawn) vs Mower & Hagerman 'rails reached Morrisville 31 Dec 1872'.
Hardwick & Woodbury passenger end 1921 rests on Fowler alone; Fowler's 1896 start disagrees by a year with the 1897 completion. A 1910s-1920s timetable or Kendall 1946 would confirm.

Omitted for lack of a dated passenger year: the 1883 Rouses Point extension (route, owner and service unsettled) and the 1980s-90s Lamoille Valley RR excursion trains (confirmed to exist, no year or segment).

St. Johnsbury - Lunenburg 1872/1877 - 1911 under the P&O/StJ&LC: whether StJ&LC trains (as well as P&O/MEC through trains) ran east of St. Johnsbury is undetermined; not drawn here (the MEC Mountain Division layer draws that track).
avg_speed_kmh and every headway_min are estimates (the StJ&LC speed is derived from one 1951 timetable column).
source_conflicts: 1912-1927 operator of St. Johnsbury - Swanton: Wikipedia (MEC lease of the whole Vermont Division) vs ICC valuation 1916 (MEC east of St. Johnsbury only).
Hardwick - Morrisville opening: ICC 1876 vs Mower & Hagerman 1872.
Hardwick & Woodbury passenger start: Fowler 1896 vs Wikipedia completion c.1 Oct 1897 (1897 drawn).

segments.note: Montpelier & St. Johnsbury Railroad, opened St. Johnsbury - Joe's Pond (West Danville) 1 Jan 1872 (ICC valuation abstract). The line was meant for Montpelier and was never built west of West Danville, where the Lamoille Valley RR turned it north-west. Danville and West Danville appear in the 1876 Pathfinder (Fowler 'y'). Operator: the constituent company until the line was jointly managed as the 'Vermont Division of the Portland & Ogdensburg Railroad' under the agreement of 21 Dec 1875; in receivership 18 Oct 1877 - 30 Jun 1880 (same railroad under receivers, not a change of operator). The St. Johnsbury & Lake Champlain took over the properties 1 Jul 1880 - service continued, see st-johnsbury-lake-champlain-main-line (ICC valuation abstract). headway_min 720 (about two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE; no 1870s timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: opening 1 Jan 1872 from the ICC valuation abstract; Danville / West Danville in the 1876 Pathfinder per Fowler, Vermont Railroads s.36. Operators and the 1 Jul 1880 handover from the ICC valuation abstract (property as of 30 Jun 1916) as read in the research report. Headway not sourced.

St. Johnsbury - Swanton: traced 95.8 mi vs documented 96.1 mi (1952 Official Guide and Fowler, Swanton milepost 96.1). Trace mileposts track the Guide closely: Greensboro 27.8 (27.8), East Hardwick 31.0 (31.0), Hardwick 34.7 (34.7), Morrisville 48.8 (48.9), Johnson 56.2 (56.4), Cambridge Jct 64.2 (64.3), Sheldon Jct 84.8 (84.6). Identical geometry to the four Portland and Ogdensburg features concatenated (Rule 4 ownership split at 1 Jul 1880). Includes ~4.7 mi around Wolcott - Morrisville on rail-trail ways lacking the operator tag. At St. Johnsbury the first ~0.6 mi (depot to the junction south of the yard) is drawn on the St. Johnsbury station/yard tracks and the Passumpsic line (Connecticut & Passumpsic Rivers, later B&M, now CP 'Lyndonville Subdivision'), which StJ&LC trains used to reach the union depot; the trail's east end is joined to that track by a 110 m synthetic link. The line starts at the exact vertex where maine_central_mountain_division.geojson ends. The west end is the StJ&LC / Central Vermont crossing at Swanton (the shared CV-owned Swanton station, ICC); the trace does not ride the CV/NECR Swanton Subdivision or the Missisquoi branch at Sheldon Junction or Cambridge Junction (0 mi on CN-tagged ways apart from a shared junction vertex at Cambridge Junction). Era: draws the alignment as abandoned c.1994 (now the rail trail); no relocation of the 1870s line was found in the research, but none was looked for, so an earlier alignment differing in detail is not excluded.

segments.note: St. Johnsbury & Lake Champlain Railroad (incorporated 31 Jan 1880) took over the Vermont Division properties and ran the trains from 1 Jul 1880 (ICC valuation abstract). Boston & Lowell, then (from 1887, as B&L lessee) Boston & Maine held a 53.4% stock control; the ICC abstract (1916) shows the StJ&LC operating its own line west of St. Johnsbury with some equipment leased from the B&M - stock control, not a change of operator, so no Rule 4 split (see not_yet_sourced for the conflicting Maine Central 1912-1927 lease claim and the 1915 'division of the Boston and Maine' obituary). Stations in the 1894 Pathfinder (Fowler 'z'). Ends at the 24 Jan 1948 reorganization as the St. Johnsbury & Lamoille County - same railroad, continued in the next segment. A single unsourced claim (VAST) that 1930s passenger service ran only Cambridge Jct - St. Johnsbury is not drawn as a gap; the 1951 Guide shows trains through to Swanton. Mixed trains count as passenger service. headway_min 480 (two to three trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE; no timetable of this era was read.
sources: Segment-level: StJ&LC takeover 1 Jul 1880 and its own operation in 1916 from the ICC valuation abstract; stations in the 1894 Pathfinder per Fowler s.36; 24 Jan 1948 reorganization from Wikipedia. Year-by-year continuity 1880-1948 and the headway are not sourced.

segments.note: Reorganized 24 Jan 1948 as the St. Johnsbury & Lamoille County Railroad - same railroad, same initials, offices and crews, so the same feature and colour (not a Rule 4 split). The Official Guide table dated 30 Sept 1951 shows westbound Nos. 71/75/51 and eastbound 52/74/76 with times, including at least one column St. Johnsbury - Swanton through (Sheldon Jct 9:40, E. Highgate 9:48, Swanton 10:15) and one terminating at Cambridge Junction; its legend includes mixed trains. Passenger service ended in 1956 (Wikipedia, american-rails.com and VTrans all give the year, VTrans tying it to the loss of the USPS mail contract); no day or month is sourced. Freight continued (state-owned 1973, Lamoille Valley RR Co. 1978 - c.1994) and is not drawn. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE from the count of three train numbers each way in the 1951 table, not all of which ran the full line.
sources: Segment-level: 1951 service with times from the 1952 Official Guide (St. Johnsbury & Lamoille County table, Sept 30 1951); 1956 end year from Wikipedia, american-rails.com and VTrans (no exact date); 1948 reorganization from Wikipedia.

segments.note: StJ&LC from 1 Jul 1880 (ICC valuation abstract). 'Maquam Bay' is in the 1881 Official Guide and 'Maquam' in the 1894 Pathfinder (Fowler 'Maquam z [Maquam Bay 1881G]'). OPEN END: 1894 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger service to Maquam stopped. Maquam is on B&M accounting-department agency lists of 1906 and 1918 and absent from 1923 (nashuacitystation.org), but an agency list is not a passenger timetable and proves nothing about passengers. Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1880 start from the ICC valuation abstract; 1881 Official Guide and 1894 Pathfinder listings per Fowler, Vermont Railroads s.36. End year is the last confirmed listing, not a sourced end. Headway not sourced.

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: no running time was read. ~15 km/h assumes a Shay-worked granite-quarry road whose passengers rode in the caboose or on bench-fitted flatcars; not sourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator='Hardwick & Woodbury Railroad' (abandoned grade, 'Hardwick-Woodbury Rail Trail', 'Fletcher Quarry Road' and untagged tracks) from the mail.ru Overpass mirror 2026-10-15 via opstrace.fetch_operator_ways, routed by opstrace.trace, Douglas-Peucker 8 m. properties.geometry_quality: Traced entirely on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Hardwick & Woodbury Railroad; no straight-line leg. Traced 7.5 mi Granite Junction - Fletcher quarry (Fletcher Quarry Road end, 44.4381N 72.4017W) vs documented ~9 mi (Fowler to 9.0; Wikipedia '9 miles mainline, including leased track') - 17% short: the quarry end and any quarry spurs beyond the mapped grade are not drawn, and which mapped end was the passenger terminus is not established. The first ~1.5 mi from Granite Junction (7 m from the main-line trace) is the StJ&LC's own Hardwick branch, leased to the H&W from 20 Apr 1896 and worked by it. Era: the grade as abandoned c.1934-40; no other alignment is known.

segments.note: Hardwick & Woodbury Railroad, its own company (not the StJ&LC) throughout its passenger years: a granite-quarry Shay road from Granite Junction, just west of Hardwick, to the Woodbury quarries, completed to the Woodbury quarry about 1 Oct 1897 (Wikipedia, citing Kendall, R&LHS Bulletin 68, 1946, and Wood, Hazen Road Dispatch 2019-20). Fowler gives passenger service '1896 > 1921'; the start is collapsed to the 1897 completion and the 1921 end rests on Fowler alone. Directly counted passenger years: 1899 (712 paying passengers), 1900 (stations in the Pathfinder, Fowler), 1906 (448 passengers) - genuine passenger traffic on a freight road, which Rule 1 counts. The StJ&LC took over operation in 1925, after the passenger end; freight to abandonment (approved Oct 1934) is not drawn. headway_min 1440 (about one trip a day) is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1896 > 1921 passenger span from Fowler, Vermont Railroads s.34; 1897 completion and the 1899/1906 passenger counts from Wikipedia (Kendall 1946; Wood 2019-20). The 1921 end has a single source. Headway not sourced.
